left.title: Purpose and benefit
items: You know the **additional requirements for business customers** and **fleets**, apply **campaigns and special conditions**, submit **special case requests** with a justification, understand **dealer assignment, validation and approval** as well as **comments** and the **Customer Account Center** (Chapter 12.1 to 12.8).

sections.head: 12.5 – 12.9 Processing
bullets: Bulk creation and validation of vehicle lists

steps: For **business customers**, enter the company name and **VAT ID** and, if applicable, the industry (12.1); for **fleets**, check the customer constellation (12.2).
Select **campaigns** or **special conditions** only if the eligibility described is met (12.3).
For deviations from the standard, submit a **special case request** with a comprehensible **justification** (12.4).
The request is assigned to the responsible **Dealer** or processor (12.5) and **validated, approved or rejected** by MO or Market (12.6).

right.text: ~~The customer group "KAM-managed key accounts" is to be used only for individual price requests~~, i.e. for KAM-managed customers or for FS 140+.

steps: Use **internal comments** for coordination and **external comments** for feedback to the customer (12.7).
Manage customer accounts and special cases in the **Customer Account Center** (12.8).
For fleets, hand vehicle lists to **bulk creation**; the system checks product, first registration and mileage per vehicle and notifies dealer, MO and MPC about the result table (12.9).

bullets: **Dealer**: special case request, campaign selection, comments
**KAM**: managed key accounts and individual price requests
Customer group "Business customer" or "KAM-managed key accounts" is selected correctly (Chapter 4.1)
Campaign eligibility is given as described
Justification for the special case is available
☐  Customer group and additional details correct
Special approvals always trigger an MO check (Chapters 6.5 and 9).
External comments are visible to the customer; do not enter internal information.
Campaigns are maintained by the Market (Chapter 14.13).

qa: When do I need a special case request?
When conditions, customer constellation or product deviate from the standard (12.4).
Who decides on the special case?
MO or Market after validation; you see the result in the application and in the comments (12.6).
What is the Customer Account Center?
The area for managing customer accounts, relationships and special cases (12.8).

Select the **tyre product** as well as **tyre type** and **tyre size** matching the vehicle (13.2).
Configure **term, mileage and scope of services** (13.3) and check **price, options and campaigns** (13.4).

right.text: ~~Tyre size and tyre type must match the vehicle equipment.~~ Deviations lead to rejection in the MO Check and prevent services from being claimed.

Tyre product is released in the market

qa: Can I combine tyres and service in one contract?
This depends on the market's product offering (Chapters 13.1 and 14.8).
Where does the tyre size come from?
From the vehicle data; check it against the actual equipment (13.2).
How are services claimed?
Via the workshop with reference to contract and coverage (13.6 and 19.9).

bullets: Tasks and scope of the Market role

bullets: Price versions, clusters and factor limits
Product change, versioning and effect on existing contracts
Vehicle groups and Van model series clustering
Product Testing as a work area
Price components, Cost Unit Split and inflation

steps: Clarify **tasks and scope** relative to the HQ role (14.1) and maintain **market-specific settings** and **country deviations** (14.2 and 14.3).
Manage **templates** (14.4) and use only the **permitted actions** in the administration area (14.5); check **visibility and authorizations** (14.6).
**Define** products, create them and **publish** them (14.8).
Maintain **price versions, clusters and factor limits** as well as **price components, Cost Unit Split and inflation** (14.9 and 14.14).

right.text: ~~Published price versions take effect immediately on new quotes.~~ Check factor limits and the effect on existing contracts in Product Testing before you publish.

steps: For **product changes**, observe **versioning** and the **effect on existing contracts** (14.10); cluster **vehicle groups** and **Van model series** (14.11).
Test changes in **Product Testing** (14.12) before you create **campaigns and discounts** (14.13).
**Check, approve and document** every change (14.7).

bullets: **Market**: product, price and campaign maintenance, administration
Blueprint and country deviations known (Chapters 15 and 20)
☐  Price version, cluster and factor limits plausible
A cluster for the relative base price requires a price factor (14.9).
Vehicle groups: the product with a current price version is preselected, expired price versions are not shown; on request the system generates name and description from the filters (14.11).
When a campaign is duplicated, the system resets the External Campaign ID; deactivated campaigns remain editable (14.13).
Depending on versioning, product changes affect only new contracts or existing contracts as well (14.10).

qa: What may the Market change without HQ?
Market-specific settings, prices, campaigns and templates within the Blueprint; deviations require HQ approval (14.3 and 15.4).
How do I test a new product?
In Product Testing with test data from Appendix I.3, before it is published (14.12).
What is a Cost Unit Split?
The split of the price into cost components, e.g. for inflation adjustments (14.14).

right.text: ~~Changes to coverage codes and SA matching affect all markets and divisions.~~ They are published only after approval and with test evidence (Chapter 16.4).

HQ role with central maintenance rights
Governance process and approval levels known (Chapter 16)
☐  Country deviation assessed and in the register
☐  Technical Options and coverage codes tested
The Blueprint is the reference for training and handbook; deviations are documented per country (Chapter 20).
Group names of technical options are unique per division; the Blueprint wizard ends with the step "Overview & Confirmation" (15.2, 15.7).
Transition modules T15-14 and T15-16 connect HQ maintenance with Market and governance.

qa: What is the Blueprint?
The global standard process with products, rules and master data from which markets may deviate only in a documented way (15.2).
Who maintains coverage codes?
HQ centrally; markets use them in product definition and claiming of services (15.7).
How do HQ and Market proceed in case of conflicts?
Via the clarification register and the governance approval (15.4 and 16.7).

left.title: Purpose and benefit
items: You observe **data protection** and safe sample data, ensure **data quality and data ownership**, use the **approval workflow**, document **test evidence**, distinguish **document management and archiving**, maintain **sources, tickets and versions** as well as the **clarification register** (Chapter 16.1 to 16.8).

left.text: References to handbook chapters and systems are highlighted; e-mail addresses are provided as links.

sections.head: 16.1 – 16.4 Data protection and quality
bullets: Data protection and safe sample data
Test evidence and productive functional baseline

sections.head: 16.5 – 16.8 Evidence
bullets: Sources, ticket references and version control

steps: Use only **safe sample data** in training, tickets and screenshots; no real customer or bank details (16.1).
Observe **data ownership** (16.2): the leading system (e.g. oneERP for customers) is authoritative; corrections are made there.
Go through the **approval workflow** (16.3): functional review, approval, documentation.
Store **test evidence** and record the **productive functional baseline** (16.4).

right.text: ~~Personal data never belongs in comments, tickets or screenshots.~~ Use the test data catalog (Appendix I.3) and anonymize examples.

steps: Distinguish **document management** (ongoing process) from **archiving** (legally secure filing) (16.5).
Maintain **sources, ticket references and versions** (16.6) and enter **contradictions and gaps** in the **clarification register** (16.7).
Ensure **dealer governance** and **reporting evidence** (16.8).

bullets: **All roles**: data protection and data quality
Knowledge of the group's data protection rules
Access to clarification register and ticket references
Archived documents are immutable; corrections create new versions.
Automated end-to-end tests for vehicle and product management are part of the test evidence per release (16.4).
The clarification register is required reading before releases (Chapter 22).

qa: May I send a screenshot with customer data to Support?
Only anonymized or with test data; real data must be redacted (16.1).
What is the difference between document management and archiving?
Document management accompanies the process; archiving is the legally secure, immutable filing (16.5).
Where do I report a contradiction in the handbook?
In the clarification register with chapter, source and ticket reference (16.7 and Appendix F).

The Market functionally, HQ for Blueprint conformity; both are documented (17.3).

Handbook, Quick Guides per chapter, knowledge checks (Appendix H) and training material in the RetailPortal.

According to the market's rollout plan; open items are tracked in the register until closed (17.5).

Only those defined in the migration scope; the rest run out in the legacy system (18.1).
What do I do with an incorrectly migrated contract?
Report the error case via the correction path; do not rebuild it manually (18.5).
When does parallel operation end?
On the cutover date defined in the cutover plan (18.6).
